site.title: Forum I · The Great Reconfiguration · Amsterdam Forum
site.description: Forum I, The Great Reconfiguration. Amsterdam, 14–15 October 2027. Philosophers, scientists, artists, founders and policymakers on the shifts reshaping power, work, cities and meaning. Keynotes, panels, film, art and food. 300 people, by invitation.

hero.eyebrow: Forum I · Amsterdam · October 2027 · 300 people · by invitation
hero.lede: Power, climate, work, cities, trust, culture, meaning and machine intelligence are moving at the same time. On stage: philosophers, scientists, anthropologists, systems thinkers, artists, founders and policymakers. Two days in Amsterdam to see these shifts as one movement, test them against people who disagree, and work out what they mean for your next decisions.

long_view.title: Every reconfiguration had its rooms.
long_view.text: The modern world was built on separations: mind from matter, economy from nature, nation from planet, human from machine. They are coming apart at once. Before, when the world rethought its foundations, small and mixed rooms helped work out what came next.

moments.title: The Axial Age
moments.text: China, India, Persia, Greece and Israel rethink what a human being is, at the same time.

moments.title: The Medici circle
moments.text: Bankers fund a philosopher to translate Plato. Poets, scholars and artists gather round. It helped shape the Renaissance.

moments.title: Descartes and Spinoza
moments.text: In the Dutch Republic, Descartes separates mind from matter. Spinoza, born in Amsterdam, answers that they are one.

moments.title: The Lunar Society
moments.text: Industrialists, scientists and philosophers at one table, once a month. It helped shape the industrial age.

moments.title: Forum I
moments.text: Our attempt at one: three hundred people, one room, the present reconfiguration.

map.title: Eight shifts. One reconfiguration.
map.intro: Each shift traces back to the same five separations the modern world was organised around. All five are failing together, and AI is speeding up every one of them.
map.outro: Forum I is built so you see this in one room, in one morning.
map.hint: Hover or tap a shift to trace it.

days.title: Two days with the people who notice change early.
days.intro: Keynotes and panels on each of the eight shifts, the evidence laid out in the Atlas, an afternoon turning it into decisions, and two evenings of film, art, food and music across the city. One room by day, one programme, no parallel tracks to miss.

movements.title: Seeing
items: **Opening keynote**: the Great Reconfiguration, and why the eight shifts are one reconfiguration.
**Keynotes and panels** on Power, Earth, Work & Wealth and Cities.
**The Atlas**: a walk-through exhibition of the evidence, open throughout both days.
**Evening**: Witness Dinners in Amsterdam houses, then the night programme: screenings, performance and music.

movements.title: Understanding
items: **Keynotes and panels** on Institutions, Culture, Meaning and Intelligence.
**The Collision**: a philosopher and a founder who disagree, on stage, about where the reconfiguration is going.
**Conversations** with people living at the edge of each shift.

movements.title: Preparing
items: **Readiness Studios** in eight domains: capital, government, cities, companies, education, culture, philanthropy, technology.
What the reconfiguration means for decisions in the next 24 months.
**Closing keynote**, the founding of the first Sensing Circles, and a closing night in the city.

leave: A Readiness Brief for your domain, plus your own page: three assumptions you're retiring.
A picture of the decade you didn't have on the way in.
A year of Weak Signal, the Forum's intelligence dispatch.
The Atlas of the Great Reconfiguration, published after the Forum.
For some, a seat in one of five Sensing Circles meeting monthly from November 2027.

speakers.title: Philosophers to founders. One stage.
speakers.intro: The shifts don't respect disciplines, so neither does the stage. Each speaker is chosen for what they have noticed, understood or lived through before it became obvious, not for the size of their title, and brings evidence, a point of view, and time for questions.

experience.title: Not only talks.
experience.intro: Some of what is changing is easier to see than to say. Around the stage, Forum I is a curated programme of art, film, food and music, made for the people in the room and commissioned around the eight shifts.

items.label: Art
items.title: Commissions
items.text: Artists commissioned to answer the eight shifts, shown inside the Atlas and around the venue.

items.label: Film
items.title: Night screenings
items.text: Short documentaries and films from the edges of each shift, with the makers in the room.

items.label: Food
items.title: The Table
items.text: Chefs cook the reconfiguration: menus built on what the world will grow, eat and waste next.

items.label: Performance
items.title: The night programme
items.text: Music, readings and performance in Amsterdam venues after the day closes, and one long-table Salon in the spirit of the Lunar Society.

items.label: Studios
items.title: Small rooms
items.text: Hands-on sessions with makers, researchers and founders: twenty people, one question, one hour.

items.label: City
items.title: Amsterdam as a case
items.text: Walks and visits to where the city is already living the shifts: water, housing, energy, food.

city.quote: Amsterdam turned openness into the first instruments of trust: the first shares, the first exchange. It is the right city to see what comes next.

different.kicker: Forum I isn't a smaller Davos. It's a different kind of room.

room.title: Three hundred people, selected for the perspectives they bring.
room.intro: Every seat is by invitation, and an invitation can't be bought. The aim is a room in which no one hears only what they already think. More than half are Fellows, who attend free: researchers, artists, younger builders and leaders from the Global South.

segments.text: Invited participants. A participation fee of €1,250, invoiced to the organisation.
Partner seats, filled with names agreed with the Curation Council.
Fellows, curated and attending free, about thirty with travel covered.

criteria: **Disciplines:** every table spans at least four sectors: business, capital, government, science, culture, civil society, the press. None is a majority.
**Geographies:** every table includes people from at least three continents. The Global South is never under-represented.
**Generations:** every table includes someone under thirty-five and someone over sixty.
**Not by payment:** Fellows, participants and partner guests sit together; no table is seated by who paid.
**Productive tension:** tables are composed to hold real disagreement, not comfort.

circles.title: Eight people. One city. Every month.
circles.text: A Sensing Circle is eight people from different worlds who meet in person, monthly, to notice what is changing before it has a name. No agenda, no presentations, no networking: a business leader, a scientist, an artist, a policymaker and others, around one table, under the Chatham House Rule.
circles.text_2: The first Circles are founded at Forum I and meet from November 2027. They are composed, not joined: nobody applies for a seat. But you can tell us where the next Circles should be, and who should sit around the table.

movement.title: What was. What is. What comes next.
movement.text: Amsterdam's three crosses stand on the city's arms, its bollards and its buildings. In ours, the third has reconfigured: two crosses for the order we inherited, a plus for what we build next.
movement.text_2: XX+ is the sign of the Great Reconfiguration, for anyone who intends to shape it rather than wait for it. Wear it, draw it, carry it. The Sensing Circles are where it meets, every month, in five cities.

invite.title: Request an invitation
invite.text_1: Tell us who you are and what you're deciding over the next two years. The Curation Council reviews every request and issues invitations in three waves through 2027.
invite.text_2: Participation is €1,250, invoiced to your organisation, and includes a year of Weak Signal. An organisation may bring up to three people and underwrites one Fellow's seat for each delegation.
invite.question: What are you deciding in the next two years that this could change?
invite.privacy: We use your details only to consider your request.
invite.thanks: Received. The Forum team will be in touch.

partner.title: Partner with Forum I
partner.text_1: Partners make the room possible and underwrite Fellows' seats. They are named across Forum I and the Atlas publication. They never buy the stage, the programme or the guest list.

tiers.name: Atlas Partner · five, one Atlas room each

partner.text_2: To protect the Forum's independence, companies developing frontier AI cannot partner. The Founding Partner closes in February 2027, the others by June.
partner.question: Why Forum I, for your organisation?
partner.privacy: We'll send the partnership prospectus and arrange a call.
partner.thanks: Received. We'll send the prospectus and propose a call.

speaker.title: Propose a speaker
speaker.text_1: We are looking for keynote speakers and panellists who see a shift before it is obvious: researchers, builders, policymakers, writers, people working inside the systems that are changing.
speaker.text_2: Propose yourself or someone else. Speakers are chosen for the strength of what they bring, not for their title. The Forum covers the travel of confirmed speakers.
speaker.question: What would they say that this room needs to hear?
speaker.privacy: We read every proposal and reply to those we take forward.
speaker.thanks: Received. Thank you. We reply to every proposal we take forward.

circle.title: Bring a Circle to your city
circle.text_1: Tell us where the next Sensing Circles should meet. We open a new city when we can compose a Circle there well: eight people whose combination creates real insight, not a peer group.
circle.text_2: Propose your city, and the people you would want around the table, including yourself. Circles are composed by the Forum; membership is by invitation and carries an annual contribution, waived for up to a third of every Circle.
circle.question: Why your city, and who should be around the table?
circle.privacy: We read every proposal and reply to those we take forward.
circle.thanks: Received. Thank you. We will be in touch when we open your city, or sooner if we have questions.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: This notice explains what the Amsterdam Forum does with personal information collected through amsforum.com and Weak Signal. The Amsterdam Forum is in formation; until its Dutch company is registered, the founder is responsible for this data.

sections.heading: What we collect
sections.text: When you send a form: your name, email address and the details you choose to give (organisation, role, country, your note). When you subscribe to Weak Signal: your email address, name, plan and when you last signed in. To stop abuse of the forms we store a shortened, one-way code of your internet address, not the address itself.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: To consider your request for an invitation, partnership or speaker proposal and reply to it; to send Weak Signal and let you sign in to read it; and to keep the site secure. We do not sell or share your details, and we do not use them for advertising.

sections.heading: Cookies
sections.text: The site uses no analytics or tracking cookies. It sets one cookie when a Weak Signal subscriber signs in (to keep you signed in for up to 60 days) and one for the site's own administrator. Both are strictly necessary.

sections.heading: Where it is kept
sections.text: On our web hosting (GoDaddy), which may store data outside the European Economic Area under its standard data-protection terms. Emails are sent through the same hosting.

sections.heading: How long
sections.text: Requests and proposals: until twelve months after Forum I, then deleted. Weak Signal subscriptions: for as long as you subscribe, and deleted within three months after it ends. You can ask us to delete your details at any time.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.text: You can ask to see, correct or delete your details, or object to how we use them, by emailing the address below. You can unsubscribe from Weak Signal from the link in every email. If you are not satisfied with our answer, you can complain to the Dutch data protection authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens).
